title: Query Complexity for Specific Function Classes (OQ-02/OQ-02)

overview.historicalContext: The study of query complexity for fixed point problems lies at the intersection of computational complexity theory, numerical analysis, and optimization. Different function classes — Lipschitz, contractive, smooth — admit fundamentally different convergence rates. Banach (1922) showed that contractions converge geometrically, while Newton's method (1669, refined by Kantorovich 1948) achieves quadratic convergence for smooth functions near simple roots. The information-theoretic lower bound shows that even with adaptive queries, binary search is optimal for the general continuous case.
overview.problemStatement:
OQ-02/OQ-02: What is the optimal query complexity for finding ε-approximate fixed points of specific function classes?

- Continuous: Θ(log(1/ε)) queries (binary search optimal)
- L-Lipschitz: Θ(log(1/ε)) queries (same as continuous)
- L-Contraction (L < 1): O(log(D/ε)/|log L|) queries (faster when L ≪ 1)
- Smooth contraction (Newton): O(log log(1/ε)) queries (quadratic convergence)
overview.text: Formalization of query complexity bounds for finding approximate fixed points across function class hierarchy: contractions (geometric convergence), Lipschitz maps (binary search), and smooth contractions (quadratic/Newton-type convergence). Proves tight bounds, information-theoretic lower bounds, and double-exponential convergence for quadratic iteration.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization builds the query complexity picture:

1. **Function classes**: Define IsLipschitzOn01, IsContractionOn01 with class hierarchy
2. **Contraction bounds**: Error bound |f^[n](x₀) - x*| ≤ L^n · D₀, plus existence of finite N
3. **Binary search**: n queries achieve 1/2^n accuracy for any continuous function
4. **Lower bound**: Information-theoretic argument — 2^n < 1/ε implies n queries insufficient
5. **Class comparison**: Contraction beats bisection when L ≤ 1/2 (L^n ≤ (1/2)^n)
6. **Quadratic convergence**: Newton-type C·|eₙ| ≤ (1/2)^(2^n) gives O(log log(1/ε))
7. **Summary**: Unified landscape theorem combining all rates
keyInsights: Binary search is universally optimal for continuous 1D functions: Θ(log(1/ε)) queries
Contractions improve on bisection when L < 1/2, with the gap widening as L → 0
Quadratic convergence (Newton-type) gives dramatic O(log log(1/ε)) improvement for smooth contractive maps
The information-theoretic lower bound Ω(log(1/ε)) applies to all function classes — even additional smoothness cannot break the barrier without contractivity

sections.title: Function Class Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsLipschitzOn01 (L-Lipschitz on [0,1]) and IsContractionOn01 (L-contraction with L < 1). Proves the inclusion: contraction ⊂ Lipschitz.

sections.title: Contraction Fixed Points
sections.summary: Proves uniqueness: an L-contraction (L < 1) has at most one fixed point. The proof uses the Lipschitz condition to derive 1 ≤ L, contradicting L < 1.

sections.title: Contraction Iteration Bounds
sections.summary: The core iteration analysis: (1) error bound $|f^n(x_0) - x^*| \leq L^n |x_0 - x^*|$ by induction, (2) ε-approximation transfer, (3) existence of finite N via $L^n \to 0$.

sections.title: Binary Search Query Count
sections.summary: Proves binary search achieves $1/2^n$ accuracy in $n$ queries via the IVT, and that each step halves the interval.

sections.title: Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
sections.summary: Proves the information-theoretic lower bound: if $2^n < 1/\varepsilon$, then $n$ queries cannot achieve $\varepsilon$-accuracy. Also proves the contrapositive: achieving $\varepsilon$-accuracy requires $2^n \geq 1/\varepsilon$.

sections.title: Class Comparisons
sections.summary: Compares convergence rates: L-contraction with L ≤ 1/2 beats bisection ($L^n \leq (1/2)^n$). Also proves $L^n \leq 1$ for any L ≤ 1.
sections.mathContext: Compares convergence rates: L-contraction with L ≤ 1/2 beats bisection ($L^n \leq (1/2)^n$). Also proves $L^n \leq 1$ for any L ≤ 1.

sections.title: Quadratic (Newton-type) Convergence
sections.summary: Formalizes quadratic convergence: if $|e_{n+1}| \leq C |e_n|^2$ and $C|e_0| \leq 1/2$, then $C|e_n| \leq (1/2)^{2^n}$. This double-exponential decay means the number of correct digits doubles per step, giving $O(\log \log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations for Newton-type methods.

sections.title: Query Complexity Landscape
sections.summary: Summary theorem unifying the query complexity picture: (1) binary search positivity, (2) contraction convergence $L^n \to 0$, (3) lower bound $2^n \geq 1$.

conclusion.summary: This formalization establishes the query complexity landscape for approximate fixed point computation across function classes. Contractions converge geometrically, with explicit iteration counts. Binary search is universally optimal at Θ(log(1/ε)) for continuous functions. Quadratic (Newton-type) convergence achieves the dramatic O(log log(1/ε)) rate for smooth contractive maps.
conclusion.implications: The hierarchy Contraction ⊂ Lipschitz ⊂ Continuous shows that stronger function class properties enable faster convergence, but the information-theoretic lower bound Ω(log(1/ε)) is universal. Only contractivity (L < 1) or smoothness (quadratic convergence) can beat the bisection rate. This connects to the PPAD-completeness result for ≥2D: even with strong function class assumptions, higher dimensions are fundamentally harder.
